# gyro_storage_bucket_website (Resource)

Publishes a bucket as a static website (https://<bucket>-<service code>.web.gyro-s3.com and connected custom domains). Creating this resource accepts the abuse rules: every object in the bucket becomes publicly readable. Destroy disables the website (the bucket and its data stay).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Single-page app (React / Vue / Angular) published from a bucket
resource "gyro_storage_bucket_website" "app" {
  service_id     = 456 # object storage service
  bucket         = gyro_storage_bucket.assets.name
  index_document = "index.html" # entry file (default index.html)
  spa            = true         # missing paths (/dashboard/settings, reloads) return index.html with 200
}

# Classic static site with its own 404 page
resource "gyro_storage_bucket_website" "docs" {
  service_id     = 456
  bucket         = "docs"
  error_document = "404.html"
}

output "app_url" { value = gyro_storage_bucket_website.app.url }
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `bucket` (String) Bucket name.
- `service_id` (Number) Object storage service id.

### Optional

- `error_document` (String) Object key of the 404 page (e.g. 404.html). Empty = plain 404. Not used while spa is true.
- `index_document` (String) Entry file name served at the root and in every folder (file name only, no /). Default index.html.
- `spa` (Boolean) Single-page app mode: every missing path returns the entry file with status 200 (client-side routing, page reloads). Real files are served as they are.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `url` (String) Website address.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <service_id>/<bucket>
terraform import gyro_storage_bucket_website.app 456/assets
```
